\difficulty{1}
Let $n\in\mathbb N$, let $\gamma$ be the standard Gaussian probability measure on
$\mathbb R^n$, and let $f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ be integrable with respect to
$\gamma$. For $(X,Y)$ distributed according to $\gamma\times\gamma$, the $L^1$ norm of
\[
f\bigl(\cos(\arccos\rho)X+\sin(\arccos\rho)Y\bigr)-f(X)
\]
tends to $0$ as $\rho\to1$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Noise difference norm bound]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.eLpNorm_gaussianNoise_sub_le}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.eLpNorm_gaussianNoise_sub_le}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.eLpNorm_integral_prod_le, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianNoise, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integrable_gaussianNoise_integrand, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.measurePreserving_gaussianEndpoint}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $\rho\in[-1,1]$, and let $f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ be
integrable with respect to the product standard Gaussian probability measure $\gamma^n$.
The $L^1(\gamma^n)$ norm of the difference between the Gaussian noise of $f$ with
parameter $\rho$ and $f$ is at most the $L^1(\gamma^n\times\gamma^n)$ norm of
$(x,y)\mapsto f(\rho x+\sqrt{1-\rho^2}\,y)-f(x)$, with the operations on vectors taken
coordinatewise.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Continuity of Gaussian rotations in $L^1$]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.tendsto_eLpNorm_gaussianEndpoint_at}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.tendsto_eLpNorm_gaussianEndpoint_at}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.measurePreserving_gaussianRotation}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n\in\mathbb N$, let $\gamma$ be the standard Gaussian probability measure on
$\mathbb R^n$, let $f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ be integrable with respect to $\gamma$,
and let $c\in\mathbb R$. For $(X,Y)$ distributed according to $\gamma\times\gamma$, the
$L^1$ norm of
\[
f\bigl(\cos(\arccos\rho)X+\sin(\arccos\rho)Y\bigr)-f\bigl(\cos(\arccos c)X+\sin(\arccos
c)Y\bigr)
\]
tends to $0$ as $\rho\to c$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Centered noise difference norm bound]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.eLpNorm_gaussianNoise_sub_mean_le}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.eLpNorm_gaussianNoise_sub_mean_le}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.eLpNorm_integral_prod_le, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianNoise, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integrable_gaussianNoise_integrand, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.measurePreserving_gaussianEndpoint}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $\rho\in[-1,1]$, and let $f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ be
integrable with respect to the product standard Gaussian probability measure $\gamma^n$.
The $L^1(\gamma^n)$ norm of the difference between the Gaussian noise of $f$ with
parameter $\rho$ and the Gaussian mean $\int f\,d\gamma^n$ is at most the
$L^1(\gamma^n\times\gamma^n)$ norm of $(x,y)\mapsto f(\rho x+\sqrt{1-\rho^2}\,y)-f(y)$,
with the operations on vectors taken coordinatewise.
\end{lemma}
